title: Put an Agent in CI Without Noisy Reviews
oneLiner: Add an agent to pull requests so it flags real defects instead of restating the diff.
audience: Solo maintainers and small teams who cannot read every automated comment.
intro: An agent in CI earns its place only if its comments change what you do. The work is mostly in the rules you give it and the files you exclude.
requirements: A CI provider that can run a CLI step on pull requests
A rules directory the agent reads on every run
A budget ceiling for model calls per pull request

sections.heading: Write the rules before the prompt
sections.body: Continue's CLI reads project rules from a directory in the repository. Put the checks you actually care about there — missing indexes, unvalidated input, missing tests — so the review is repeatable and versioned with the code.

sections.heading: Review the diff, not the repository
sections.body: Scope the job to changed files. A repository-wide review on every pull request produces a wall of pre-existing findings that nobody reads and that hides the new defect.

sections.heading: Cap the output
sections.body: Ask for a short checklist with file and line references, and fail the check only on rules you marked blocking. Advisory findings belong in a comment, not a red build.

sections.heading: Measure the noise
sections.body: Track how many comments were acted on over two weeks. If the answer is close to zero, the rule set is wrong — tighten it or remove the job.

checklist: Rules live in the repository and are reviewed like code.
Blocking rules are separated from advisory notes.
Comment usefulness is reviewed on a fixed cadence.
